beats.story: The day after my thirty-third birthday, I wake up with a stiffness in my limbs so intense I'm certain I actually died and my body has begun rigor mortis. The sun is far too bright, and my brain bangs against my skull. Pain seems to reach into me from another realm. It's like everything -- all the booze, the workdays, and a lifetime of angst -- has taken literal bites out of me. In short, it's not a great way to wake up. I clear my throat in a failed attempt to clear the sawdust coating the inside of it. Then last night comes rushing back. I remember running into Miley.
beats.story_cn: 三十三岁生日的第二天醒来，我四肢僵硬得像真死了，尸体正开始经历尸僵。阳光刺眼得恶毒，脑浆在头骨里横冲直撞。疼痛从异次元刺穿我——仿佛所有这些：酒、工作日、一辈子的焦虑症，都对我完成了真实的啃噬。简而言之，这绝非理想的苏醒方式。我清了清嗓子，试图清除喉管里那层粗砂纸般的滞涩感，却徒劳无功。接着昨夜的记忆如潮倒灌，我记起撞见米莉的那个瞬间。

beats.story: Did I scar her? Again? I roll sideways, and the cool corner of my phone presses against my temple. I try not to think about all the cancer waves it must've seeded in my brain as I slept. The damn thing looks like a little shit; fingerprints dance all over it like it's been partying. On the inside, I'm sure it's laughing at all the things it's seen me do. It deserves to. When I grab it, the screen lights up and displays the message I sent to Armin.
beats.story_cn: 我又给她留下伤疤了吗？再次？我侧身翻倒，冰凉的手机棱角抵住太阳穴。尽量不去想这玩意儿整夜在我脑里埋下了多少癌细胞波纹。该死的小东西看着就像个混蛋；指纹在上面狂欢起舞，仿佛刚开完派对。我敢肯定它内在正嘲笑着目睹过的所有蠢事——它完全有资格如此。当我抓起它时，屏幕亮起，显出我发给阿明的那条信息。

beats.story: Shit. I fly into an upright position and blink the screen into focus. Five minutes after I sent it, he read it, yet there's no reply. I should get rid of my phone. I should drag my body into the tub and hate myself there for a while, but the cool comforter between my legs is all I have left. I stare at the wall, at the power outlet that seems to be making a "wow" face at me, when my phone chimes with the noise that means my mom wants to FaceTime. If I ignore her, she'll just show up in person. So I hold the phone up to my face and hit accept.
beats.story_cn: 该死。我猛地坐直，眨着眼让屏幕对焦。我发出信息五分钟他就读了，却毫无回音。我该扔掉手机。该把自己拖进浴缸，在那里痛恨自己片刻，但双腿间冰凉的被褥是我仅剩的慰藉。我盯着墙壁，盯着那个仿佛正对我做“哇哦”表情的电源插座——这时手机突然响起那个代表妈妈要视频通话的提示音。若我无视，她绝对会亲自登门。于是我将手机举到脸前，按下了接听。

beats.story: Mom's already scowling as the call connects, and in the corner of the screen, I can see why: my eyes are bloodshot and ringed with smudged mascara. I tilt the camera away, but it isn't fast enough. "Why don't you wash your face anymore? This will give you wrinkles, and you're getting older now." "I forgot." My voice is gravelly and worn. "I was having dinner late with friends." It's not lost on me that there was once a time I would lie to my mom that I was "staying in," and how pathetic this new brand of deception is. "I hope you didn't drink and drive. Stop showing me your ceiling -- I call to see your face." There's a hollow hitch in her voice. She's no stranger to wine herself.
beats.story_cn: 视频刚接通妈妈就在皱眉，屏幕角落我明白了原因：眼睛布满血丝，睫毛膏晕成黑圈。我急忙转动镜头却为时已晚。“怎么连脸都不洗？会长皱纹的，你现在年纪可不小了。”“忘了。”我的声音沙哑疲惫，“和朋友晚餐吃晚了。”我清晰记得曾几何时，我对妈妈撒谎说“宅家”，而如今这种新型谎言何其可悲。“希望你没酒后驾车——别老对着天花板，我打电话是想看你的脸。”她声音里藏着空洞的哽咽。她自己对葡萄酒也并不陌生。

beats.story: People underestimate how traumatic it is to leave a country because it dramatically changed overnight. How messed up it is to start a new life in a place where a good portion of the people will hate you for simply being there. My mouth and tongue sour against themselves. "I don't drive." "Did you do kosbazi with someone? Is that why your makeup is on?" The hope in her eyes is the worst. "No, Mom, my kos was empty the whole night." We only use Farsi words for the sex talk. She tsks me again, but through a feat of great restraint, she doesn't push the issue. "How's work?" she asks.
beats.story_cn: 人们总低估背井离乡的创伤性——整个世界一夜倾覆，而你要在新天地从头开始，偏偏那里半数人会因你存在本身而憎恶你。我的舌根泛起酸苦。“我不开车。”“你跟谁搞过 kosbazi（波斯俚语：性行为）吗？所以才化妆？”她眼里的期盼最是折磨。“没有，妈妈，我整晚都 empty（空虚/未发生）。”我们只用波斯语谈性事。她又啧了一声，但凭惊人的克制力没再追问。“工作怎样？”她问。

beats.story: "Good, good!" My voice is too pitchy. To drive it home, I say, "My job seems very secure." There's nothing more important to my mother than my financial security. For years I've been sugarcoating everything about that job to make it seem like a bigger deal than it is. "Good. Maybe you'll get a promotion." "If one comes up, I can't see why not." I don't dwell on how far outside the realm that is. I'm once again thankful I didn't lose my job yesterday. The trauma that would cause my mom would be too much. When I was a child and we were shopping for school supplies, she told me I didn't need an eraser, I just shouldn't make mistakes.
beats.story_cn: “挺好挺好！”我的声调过于高亢。为加强说服力，我补上一句：“工作看着挺稳。”对我妈而言，没有什么比我的经济保障更重要。这些年来，我把那份工作美化得天花乱坠，仿佛它比我实际的价值重要得多。“挺好。说不定能升职。”“如果有空缺，我看没理由不行。”我绝口不提这离现实有多遥远。再次庆幸昨天没丢工作，否则对母亲的打击将是灭顶之灾。儿时陪她买学习用品，她说我不需要橡皮，只因我根本不该犯错。

beats.story: My gaze drifts to the wall again, thick and milky from several layers of paint meant to wash over each previous tenant's emotional baggage. Maybe it doesn't look that great to an outside observer, but the life I've built here in my apartment is everything compared with what it was when I was living with my parents. Here, I'm free to drink and watch whatever I want and not be perceived with disapproval 24/7. I don't have to feel like a failure all the time, and when I do, it's on my terms. But if I lost my job, those threatening letters from Marty would become actionable in a matter of just a few days. I'd have no choice but to move back in with Mom and Dad. "Keep working hard and they'll notice." Mom smiles, though the top half of her face remains still due to a healthy dose of Botox. But she seems to look deeper into the camera.
beats.story_cn: 目光再次飘向墙面——层层油漆厚如凝脂，企图覆盖前任租客所有情绪残渣。外人看来或许平平无奇，但在这间公寓构建的生活，相比与父母同住时已是云泥之别。在此我能自在饮酒观影，不必承受全天候的批判凝视。不必时刻自觉失败，即便偶尔颓丧，也是自主承受。可若失业，马蒂那些威胁信函几日内便会化为实质行动。我将别无选择，只能搬回父母家。“继续好好干，他们总会看见。”妈妈微笑，肉毒杆菌让她的上半张脸僵如面具，但她仿佛透过屏幕凝视着更深处。

beats.story: "You sure you're okay?" "Oh yeah." I nod way too hard. "Where's Dad?" Her gaze shifts. "Putting on his shoes. The ugly man drove his car over a curb, so he has to get it fixed -- " "Happy birthday, Jolene," he pipes in from the background, followed by a throat clearing. A hand holding one shoe appears to wave on the screen. "Thanks." I wave back, my hand as stiff as his voice. Speaking to him always leaves me hollow and splintered. Ever since I overheard him seven years ago: "She's twenty-five and she's a dependent still.
beats.story_cn: “你确定没事？”“哦没事。”我点头幅度大得失控。“爸爸呢？”她眼神飘忽。“在穿鞋。那丑男人开车冲上路沿，得去修——”“生日快乐啊乔琳，”背景里突然插入他的声音，接着是清嗓子的响动。一只拎着皮鞋的手在屏幕前挥了挥。“谢谢。”我回挥手，手掌与他嗓音同样僵硬。每次和他通话都让我感到空洞破碎，自从七年前我无意听闻：“她二十五了还靠我们养活。”

beats.story: She doesn't have a life yet; she won't even make friends." Shame flushed every inch of my skin, and a few weeks later I moved out. If Mom wasn't around, we'd only see each other for a sad Christmas dinner. As the screen shifts back to Mom's face, there's a moment of silence that nobody can fill. Here is the part where I should ask about the aunties. Except there are usually at least two whom she's not on speaking terms with at any given time and mentioning the wrong one could set the mood off. "Well, thanks for calling." "Happy birthday. Once Daddy fixes the car, we take you for dinner tonight? I'll come pick you up." I practically yell, "No!" There's no way they're coming here.
beats.story_cn: “她还没学会生活；连朋友都不会交。”羞耻感像沸水烫过皮肤般蔓延，几周后我搬离了家。若母亲不在，我们仅会在凄清的圣诞晚餐上见一面。当镜头切回母亲脸庞时，空气里弥漫着无人能填补的沉默。此刻本该问问姨妈们的情况。可她们中总有至少两人在冷战，提错名字便会让气氛急转直下。“那么，谢谢来电。”“生日快乐。等爸爸修好车，今晚接你去吃饭？我来接你。”我几乎是吼出：“不行！”他们绝不能来这里。

beats.story: I need twenty business months to make it presentable. She huffs. "I'll only come for a minute. I have to meet Kumar near you. I need more saffron." My stomach clenches as I take in the mess of bottles and clothes strewn around the apartment. "I thought your saffron dealer was in Inglewood?" Even though there are quite a few Persian markets in town, Mom gets most of her specialty groceries via a network of dealers sprinkled across the city due to "better pricing and quality." It's all very tough to track. "I stopped going to Peyman. He's cheapskate and his saffron is no good anymore." It's best not to get into it.
beats.story_cn: “我需要二十个工作日才能收拾体面。”她冷哼道，“我只待五分钟。要去你家附近见库马尔，我得买更多藏红花。”望着公寓里散落的瓶罐与衣物，我胃部一阵紧缩。“我记得你的藏红花供应商在英格尔伍德？”尽管城里有好几家波斯市场，但母亲通过散布全城的特殊供货网络采购特产食材——据她说是“价格更优品质更好”。整套流程简直像地下交易。“我不找佩曼了，那吝啬鬼的藏红花质量早不行了。”最好别深究。

beats.story: "Mom, I'm really not feeling well and won't be good for a visit. I think I'm getting a migraine." Her disapproving gaze churns the acid in my stomach. "You haven't let me see you in very long time. I didn't move to not see you and only visit my same old relatives, when Minoo is always bitch." My parents are social people, and after high school, while I stayed holed up in the basement, Mom and Dad were still attempting to venture into our too-small town. But they were disgraced by proxy in every way. Dad worked as a chemical engineer at the same company as my friend Ellie's dad. In fact, my dad reported directly to Mr. Wong.
beats.story_cn: “妈，我真不舒服，没法接待你。估计是偏头痛犯了。”她不赞同的目光搅得我胃里泛酸。“你太久没让我见你了。我搬来又不是为了只见老亲戚——明整天就知道抱怨！”我父母是社交达人，高中毕业后我躲地下室里，他们仍试图融入这个小镇，却因我蒙受百般屈辱。父亲在好友艾莉父亲的同一家化工厂当化学工程师，实际上直接向黄先生汇报。

beats.story: And after everything happened, Dad's career crumbled at the same rate the wall between me and him solidified. Two years later, he retired in shame, and for seven years we were the town pariahs, living in purgatory under one roof. When I finally took the online courses for business administration, finally got an interview at Supershops, and finally moved two hours away from that town, it became obvious that my parents would leave too. There was nothing holding them there anymore. They came to Calgary, and Mom's been trying to convince me to move back in with them ever since. It always sounds innocent -- "Save money for a house or wedding" -- but the real tone of it all is that I'm supposed to want a house and wedding. The guilt of everything I did to them would be enough, but add to that the pressure of the life they want for me, and every conversation we have is the worst. "We can have dinner another night, I promise, when I'm better," I say before thinking too hard.
beats.story_cn: 一切崩塌之后，父亲的职业生涯以我们之间那堵高墙凝固的同等速度瓦解。两年后他蒙羞退休，而我们沦为小镇弃民，在同一屋檐下活了七年的人间炼狱。当我终于修完工商管理网课，终于在“超级商城”拿到面试机会，终于搬离小镇两小时车程外，父母显然也将随之离开。他们在那里已无任何牵挂。他们来到卡尔加里，母亲便开始不断劝我搬回去同住。她总说得很无辜——“省点钱买房或者结婚吧”——但话语底下暗涌的真意是：我该渴望房子与婚姻。我曾对他们造成的愧疚已足够沉重，再叠加上他们为我规划的人生期许，每一次对话都成了炼狱般的煎熬。“改天一起吃饭吧，我保证，等我状态好些。”我未及深思便匆匆说道。

beats.story: The twist in Mom's smile sends a shudder through me. "Oh! Why not come to dinner with the aunties this week? They all can wish you happy birthday." That would be entering the lion's den. Every Monday, my mom meets some local Persian ladies for half-price kabob and even cheaper gossip. As soon as my parents moved to town, Mom's social life somehow became livelier than mine. They try to convince their kids to come, but rarely will one of us cousins be emotionally stable enough to agree to such a thing. I'm about to pull out the excuses, but Mom's eyes glint back, hopeful.
beats.story_cn: 母亲笑容里的微妙转折让我脊背生寒。“哦！这周何不和阿姨们一起吃晚饭？她们都该祝你生日快乐呢。”那简直是踏入狮穴。每周一，母亲都会和几位当地波斯女士聚会，享受半价烤肉与更廉价的八卦。自从父母搬到镇上，母亲的社交生活竟诡异地比我还要鲜活。她们总试图说服子女参加，但鲜少有哪个表亲能精神稳定到答应这种事。我正要搬出借口，母亲眼中却闪起期盼的光。

beats.story: "Okay," I blurt out. Her smile wrinkles her whole face. "Ey jan. Remember to do your makeup pretty. I want to be proud that you came out of my kos." "Will do, and thanks for that birthday image. I should tidy up." "Good girl. You should leave the apartment and make sure you get some sun on your skin." She makes a gesture to look behind me. "It's so dusty and dark, I don't know why you need to live there." Just like that, guilt is replaced with a deeper irritation branded specifically for her.
beats.story_cn: “好。”我脱口而出。她的笑容在整张脸上漾开皱纹。“哎呀，记得把妆画漂亮点。我要为你从我子宫里出来感到骄傲。”“遵命，谢谢您这份生日‘意象’。我得收拾一下了。”“乖女儿。你该离开公寓，晒晒太阳。”她扭头瞥向我身后，“这儿又暗又积灰，真不懂你为何偏住这儿。”愧疚就这样被更灼人的烦躁取代——这烦躁专为她而生。

beats.story: "Talk soon." "Eat some fruit," Mom says as a goodbye. After letting her go, I spend a good ten minutes zoning out on my phone. I end up watching a disappointing proposal video with cue cards and then reading a clickbait mess of different ways people were caught in lies. Finally, I'm disgusted with myself enough to shuffle unsteadily off the couch, my every move heating my head. I peel off my dad's old company shirt and shimmy out of my underwear. The cool porcelain of the empty bath softens the wooziness. I twist the tap with my foot, and as the bath fills, I search YouTube, and then the whole room is filled with the song that was playing when Ellie died. I sing along.
beats.story_cn: “再聊。”“吃点水果。”母亲以这句话作别。挂断后，我对着手机怔忡了整整十分钟。先是看了一段令人失望的求婚视频——对方举着提示卡；又读了几篇诱饵文章，尽是些人们谎言败露的狗血故事。最终，自我厌恶驱使我踉跄离开沙发，每个动作都让头部阵阵发热。我剥下父亲的旧公司衬衫，褪下内裤。空浴缸冰凉的陶瓷质地缓解了眩晕。我用脚拧开水龙头，当水渐渐注满时，我打开YouTube，整个房间顿时回荡起艾莉去世时那首歌的旋律。我跟着唱起来。

beats.story: It's a sick thing I don't know how to stop forcing myself to do. Before I can even finish a thought, giant tears stream down my face and glob at my cheeks. And they feel like home. I didn't even go to her funeral. It was the right move. When the song ends, I hit play again. Because if Ellie hadn't been friends with me, there wouldn't have been a funeral at all.
beats.story_cn: 这是种病态，我却不知如何停止强迫自己这么做。思绪尚未完整，滚烫的泪珠已奔涌而出，凝在脸颊。它们却让我感到像回到了家。我甚至没去参加她的葬礼。这是对的。当歌曲结束，我按下重播键。因为若非艾莉曾与我为友，本就不会有葬礼存在。
